headline: Kai, everything November beat up is bouncing at once — chips, gold, bitcoin — and the half-day tape gives it three and a half hours to stick.
subline: Nasdaq futures are up 2.4% into a 1 p.m. close, December-hike odds sit at 100%, and tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz keep oil and gold bid.
asof: Pre-market futures · as of 6:45 AM ET Friday · stocks close 1 p.m., bonds 2 p.m. ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Semis lead a broad pre-market bounce
items.sentence: Nvidia rose nearly 4% and Micron 6% before the bell as AI-profitability jitters eased into the holiday-shortened session, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: December hike odds pinned at 100%
items.sentence: CME FedWatch has had a December 9 hike at 100% for about two weeks, with 64% odds the target range reaches 4.25%–4.50% by the January meeting, per The Motley Fool.

items.title: Oil firm on Saudi and Hormuz attacks
items.sentence: WTI rose 2.43% to $85.71 and Brent traded near $92 a barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure escalated, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Bank of Korea hikes on an AI chip boom
items.sentence: South Korea's central bank raised interest rates and lifted its GDP growth forecast, crediting the AI chip demand powering its exporters, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Bitcoin claws back to $61,780
items.sentence: Bitcoin rose 8% from Wednesday's $57,300 low to $61,780 — still down 20% this November — a thin-volume rebound Yahoo Finance ties to a softer dollar.

items.title: Tankers hit near Hormuz as war widens
items.sentence: Two of three tankers struck near Oman's Khasab caught fire after hitting naval mines and a third was hit by an unknown projectile, Al Jazeera reports, citing Iran's IRGC.

items.title: Kim orders wider tactical nuclear deployment
items.sentence: Kim Jong Un said North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nuclear weapons, calling attempts to deny its nuclear status an "open declaration of war," per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Black Friday opens a $1 trillion season
items.sentence: Shoppers hit the stores this morning in a year the National Retail Federation forecasts the first $1 trillion US holiday season, per Retail TouchPoints.

items.title: Ukrainian drones kill five in occupied Zaporizhia
items.sentence: A Ukrainian drone attack killed five people in the Russian-occupied Zaporizhia region, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Thirteen dead in Indonesian gold mine flood
items.sentence: At least 13 people died when a gold mine flooded in West Java, where rescue efforts continue, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Nvidia cuts half its Asian buyers loose
items.sentence: Nvidia removed more than half of its Asian customers from its approved-buyer whitelist as Washington's China-diversion crackdown widens, per The Next Web.

items.title: Singapore seeks talks over US chip rules
items.sentence: Singapore is seeking talks with Washington over the new AI chip export rules amid fallout from the Nvidia scandal and the Megaspeed probe, per the South China Morning Post.

items.title: Amodei: "absurd" that Anthropic wants AI in charge
items.sentence: Dario Amodei called it "absurd" to suggest he wants humans to surrender free will to AI, pushing back on an Axios report and rival jabs in a lengthy X post, per Euronews.

items.title: CISA orders patch for exploited Drupal flaw
items.sentence: CISA ordered federal agencies to patch an actively exploited Drupal vulnerability — a flaw SecurityWeek says was first flagged by Anthropic's AI code scanner — per BleepingComputer.
